sources.entry: PiPifier - PiPifier is a native macOS 10.12 Safari extension that lets you use every HTML5 video in Picture in Picture mode.

summary.one_liner: PiPifier is a native macOS and iOS Safari extension that enables Picture-in-Picture mode for any HTML5 video on a web page, including sites like YouTube that block the native controls.
summary.what_it_does: On macOS, a toolbar icon in Safari turns on Picture-in-Picture for the HTML5 video on the current page. On iOS, it runs as a Share-menu Action Extension ("Run PiPifier") that does the same thing. The README says the user must interact with the video once (for example play or pause) before activating it, and that the macOS extension must be enabled in Safari's Extensions preferences. The README states the iOS version exists because some sites hide the default iOS video controls, so PiP cannot be started normally; PiPifier is meant to work around that. The README does not describe any other features.
use_cases: Watch YouTube videos in picture-in-picture while using other apps
Float an HTML5 video over other windows on a Mac
Enable picture-in-picture on iPhone or iPad for sites that block native PiP
Keep a video playing in a small window while browsing
how_to_run: macOS: install PiPifier from the Mac App Store and launch it once
macOS: in Safari, open Preferences > Extensions and enable PiPifier
macOS: use View > Customize Toolbar to drag the PiPifier icon to the toolbar
macOS: interact with the video once, then press the PiPifier toolbar icon
iOS: install PiPifier from the App Store, open Safari's Share menu, choose More, and enable 'Run PiPifier'
iOS: on a page with a video, choose 'Run PiPifier' from the Share menu
stack: Swift/Xcode (implied by 'latest Xcode' requirement for development)
notable: Works on any HTML5 video, not only sites with built-in PiP support
Provides both a macOS Safari toolbar extension and an iOS Share-menu action extension
Free to download from the Mac App Store and the App Store
Targets sites such as YouTube that hide native iOS video controls
caveats: Requires macOS 10.12 or later, and iPad with iOS 10 or iPhone with iOS 14 or later
The video must be interacted with once before PiP can be enabled; autoplaying videos may need a pause and play
Building from source requires the latest Xcode and signing the extension, or allowing unsigned extensions in Safari's Developer menu
